evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The GUI-exposed naming_pattern must either be wired into branch generation with documented placeholders or kept hidden/inert until branch-generation support lands.
canonical_text: The nothing to commit case may be detected and logged as informational without masking real git command failures.
canonical_text: Source Control > Worktrees presents first-class worktree topology, filters, graph badge, command-backed events, disabled reasons, and stale-group defaults.

items.impact: The units define strong branch, commit, logging, and Source Control policies, but their repeated acceptance criteria primarily prove migration addressability and preservation; they do not specify executable runtime or GUI assertions for ignored naming fields, stale topology, disabled reasons, or false classification of real Git failures.
items.statement: Branch strategy and naming have an SSOT and the GUI must not imply unsupported naming behavior; commit/logging behavior and Source Control ownership/topology are also explicit. The adversarial gap is the lack of behavior-level oracles that distinguish supported, stale, disabled, and genuinely failed states.
items.title: Branch and Source Control policies lack behavior-level oracles

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Worktree action menus and blocked cards enforce lineage-safe prune/remove/reuse/recover with disabled explanations and exact recovery targeting.
canonical_text: Conflict assistant provides guided merge, rebase/worktree, and worktree-conflict repair through Source Control while preserving explicit approval and separate resolution records.

canonical_text: "Every GUI setting that changes runtime behavior, including interview execution-affecting settings, HITL node toggles, Git enablement, branching fields, and per-provider concurrency caps, belongs in the run-start config snapshot rather than GUI-only state."

items.impact: A run can observe a mixed configuration if GUI edits race with snapshot construction, and destructive or recovery actions can present stale enablement if lineage changes after rendering. No revision, atomic capture boundary, compare-and-swap rule, or revalidation-at-action contract is stated.
items.statement: The window establishes safe actions, advisory AI batching, review identity, explicit conflict approval, Option B config wiring, and complete run-start projection. It does not define atomic snapshot semantics or mandatory last-moment lineage revalidation for concurrent GUI and repository changes.
items.title: Config snapshot and action enablement are not concurrency-safe by contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Implementation sequencing keeps Phase 1 config wiring before worktree/Git phases, Phase 3.1 git binary resolution before worktree merge checks, and Phase 5 tests after Phase 2 and Phase 3 implementation behavior exists."

canonical_text: "Phase 5 testing and acceptance require config wiring tests, worktree lifecycle tests, Git integration tests, GUI handler tests, and acceptance criteria proving GUI settings affect runtime, worktrees are tracked, and Git/PR operations use configured policy."

items.impact: A builder can satisfy the named test categories with shallow happy-path checks. The plan does not require failure injection for config discovery, Git/API errors, path-safety rejection, conflict persistence, GUI stale-state behavior, or recovery after partial operations.
items.statement: The implementation order and five phase checklists are explicit, including broad test families. Their test contract remains category-level rather than falsifiable at the important partial-failure and stale-state seams.
items.title: Phase acceptance names test families without adversarial cases

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Config schema migration introduces a single canonical BranchGranularity enum, migrates legacy strings, exposes push_policy and merge_policy, and discloses Save timing so GUI edits apply to current run start while persistence applies to next launch."

canonical_text: "Conflict worktree persistence may be in-memory for the initial release, while longer-lived conflict state records use worktree-conflicts.json or canonical storage without conflating conflict cleanup with normal worktree cleanup."

items.impact: The initial-release allowance for in-memory conflict worktrees has no explicit crash boundary, promotion trigger, restart reconstruction behavior, retention/deletion rule, or reconciliation procedure when file and canonical storage disagree. A restart can lose actionable conflict context or expose stale recovery rows.
items.statement: The window usefully fixes required versus optional scope, enum migration, selected-project config discovery, conflict cleanup separation, and Git binary/API policy. Conflict state durability across process failure and storage migration remains under-specified.
items.title: Conflict persistence has no restart or reconciliation contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "active_worktrees is repopulated from listed worktree paths by extracting node identity and inserting canonical entries rather than relying on stale in-memory state."

canonical_text: "Resolved worktree decisions require HashSet<node_id> active tracking, detached HEAD merge handling, recovery timing, and Windows-safe path behavior for worktree lifecycle implementation."

items.impact: Path-derived node identity is an untrusted reconstruction input. Without a canonical grammar, collision rule, malformed-path disposition, repository binding check, and duplicate-entry reconciliation, restart repopulation can attach the wrong node to a worktree or silently omit one, especially across Windows path forms and detached HEAD states.
items.statement: Restart repopulation, granularity/strategy separation, integration setup, repository-scoped Doctor checks, and resolved Git/config decisions are explicit. The canonical identity and error contract for path-derived repopulation is not.
items.title: Path-derived worktree identity lacks validation and collision rules

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Worktree-native safe points and retry visibility record scoped filesystem/Git state, avoid destructive reset behavior, expose retry posture, and provide acceptance criteria for safe-point creation/restoration and conflict-aware retry disclosure."
canonical_text: "Safe point and worktree recovery alignment requires worktree-specific baselines, explicit recovery targets, and dirty/conflict blocking before mutation or recovery action proceeds."

items.impact: Safe-point creation or restoration can fail after only part of filesystem or Git state changes. The plan does not define captured contents, atomic commit markers, integrity/version checks, retention, concurrent mutation exclusion, idempotent retry, or recovery from a failed restore, leaving destructive outcomes to builder discretion.
items.statement: DRY ownership, canonical crew/lifecycle state, non-destructive safe points, explicit targets, and dirty/conflict blocking are all required. The transactional and lifecycle contract for safe-point data itself is absent.
items.title: Safe-point recovery lacks an atomic transaction and failure contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Worktree allocation is package/lane based: Orchestrator owns the active run lane-pool truth while Source Control owns repo/worktree execution and inspection, and old run/tier/subtask allocation patterns are compatibility context until mapped to package lane pools."

canonical_text: "Cross-lane reuse requires contamination checks, contamination-triggered shrink, per-package lane ceilings, lane-named worktrees, preview-heavy archive/remove operations, split Orchestrator versus Source Control action ownership, and package/lane policy as the scale owner."

items.impact: The scale owner and qualitative controls are named, but no ceiling derivation, allocation fairness, contention order, stale-lease accounting, contamination shrink threshold, or race-resolution rule is defined. Orchestrator and Source Control can therefore disagree about capacity or ownership during concurrent allocate/archive/remove flows.
items.statement: The window clearly separates conflict cleanup, lane-pool truth, Source Control action ownership, compatibility identity, and preview-heavy destructive operations. It leaves capacity calculation and concurrent cross-owner arbitration unspecified.
items.title: Package-lane scale policy has no capacity or arbitration algorithm

evidence.exact_quote: Source Control and Worktrees must surface GoalRun and WorkNode write-surface policy through worktree leases, isolated writes, parent merge, blocked write reasons, and write-mode labels. Supported labels include read_only, proposal_only, patch_only, isolated_worktree, leased_writer, and parent_writer. Subagents must not mutate overlapping live surfaces concurrently, and every GoalRun write-capable action must preserve worktree_id, owner lane, and lease or blocker evidence.

Mutation-capable WorkNode attempts must run in a known repo/worktree context. Parallel WorkNodes require isolated worktrees or explicit clean allocation, and dirty, conflicted, contaminated, blocked-preserved, or lineage-mismatched worktrees cannot be reused silently. Worktree allocation records preserve repo_id, worktree_id, worktree_path, baseline_commit_oid, branch/head state, head_commit_oid, changed_files, conflict_refs, owner lane, lease state, dirty_state_policy, conflict_policy, merge_policy, github_policy, rollback_available, rollback_ref, and restore_command_or_action. Local source-control/worktree state remains execution truth; GitHub is an optional promotion/output layer when configured.
- Never silently commit, stash, discard, reset, or overwrite user changes.

items.impact: The write-mode and worktree record vocabulary is strong, but lease acquisition, renewal, expiry, revocation, fencing, abandoned-writer recovery, clock/partition behavior, and atomic persistence of allocation plus receipt evidence are unspecified. Two actors can believe they hold authority, or a mutation can occur without a durable matching receipt after partial failure.
items.statement: The retired bridge is correctly non-product lineage, while the addenda establish package/lane allocation, visible write modes, local execution truth, unsafe-reuse blocking, permissioned planning actions, and preservation of user changes. The concurrency and durability semantics that make leases and receipts authoritative are missing.
items.title: Worktree leases and mutation receipts lack fencing and atomic durability

Reviewed W-039 through W-044 for phase dependency order, implementation checklists, GUI scope, and adversarial test falsifiability.
Reviewed W-045 through W-051 for source hints, required scope, migration, project context, conflict persistence, and Git binary/API constraints.
Reviewed W-052 through W-058 for repopulation identity, strategy/granularity, Git tests, Doctor scope, cross-platform recovery, and resolved decisions.
Reviewed W-059 through W-064 for DRY ownership, crew/lifecycle canon, safe points, retry visibility, recovery targets, and partial-failure safety.
Reviewed W-065 through W-069 for conflict canon, package/lane ownership, route identity, cross-lane reuse, destructive-action previews, and scale arbitration.
